title: Package a Node CLI with a bin field and shebang
when: A Node command line tool works locally and the user wants it installable as a command, with only the needed files in the package and a shebang that works everywhere.
prompt:
Goal: A package that installs a working command on linux, mac and win32, holds only runtime files and was tested from the packed tarball.
Steps:
1. bin/tool.mjs: line 1 #!/usr/bin/env node with LF endings; mode 755 via chmod +x, or git update-index --chmod=+x when committing from win32.
2. package.json: name, version, "type": "module", "bin": { "tool": "bin/tool.mjs" }, "files": ["bin", "src", "README.md", "LICENSE"], "engines": { "node": ">=20" }, license, "scripts": { "test": "node --test" }.
3. --version reads package.json through createRequire(import.meta.url)("../package.json").version.
4. bin/tool.mjs stays tiny: import main from ../src/main.mjs, run it, set process.exitCode.
5. Run the package manager's pack command in dry run mode and read the file list: no tests, fixtures, .env or editor folders.
6. Real install test: pack to a .tgz, install it globally into a temp prefix, run tool --help and one real command, uninstall.
7. Publishing needs a registry account with two factor auth.
Quality bar:
- The tarball holds only runtime files.
- The command works from any folder after install.
Pitfalls:
- A CRLF shebang from a win32 editor: "No such file or directory".
- No "files" list, shipping test data and secrets.
- bin pointing at a file missing from "files".
Verify:
- [ ] Shebang on line 1.
- [ ] package.json valid with bin, files and engines.
- [ ] Packed contents reviewed.
- [ ] Installed command answers --help.
Output: package.json, bin/tool.mjs, src/main.mjs and an Install section in README.md.

examples.input: quero instalar minha CLI como comando global
examples.output: package.json with bin, files and engines, LF shebang in bin/tool.mjs, packed tarball inspected and installed into a temp prefix
